description: Kick drum voice with its own sixteen-step Euclidean pattern and an accent envelope that has to open before anything is heard

params.text: Sets what share of the sixteen steps carry a kick, 0% to 100%
Chooses which of every four clocks fires the accent envelope, counting from 1 to 7 round the four
Sets how long the accent envelope takes to fall, 10ms to 2 seconds
Sets the pitch of the sine oscillator, 24Hz to 500Hz
Sets how far the pitch envelope sweeps the oscillator, up to twenty octaves above the TUNE setting at the top of its travel
Drives the sine into a saturator, leaving it alone at the bottom of its travel and folding it towards a square at the top
Sets how long both of the kick's envelopes take to fall, 10ms to 2 seconds
Bends the fall of the pitch envelope: at the bottom of its travel it collapses almost at once, at the top it falls close to a straight line

inputs.text: Each rising edge above 1V advances the sixteen-step pattern and the four-step accent count
Added to the TUNE knob, one volt per octave; the pitch is held between 24Hz and 500Hz
Added to the FM knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the PUNCH knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the DECAY knob, a tenth of a second per volt; the total is held between 10ms and 2 seconds
Added to the FILL knob, 10% per volt; the total is held between 0% and 100%

outputs.text: The kick's amplitude envelope, 0V to 10V, rising in 1ms and falling in the time set by DECAY
The pitch envelope, 0V to 10V, bent by SHAPE
The kick itself, the saturated sine through both the amplitude envelope and the accent envelope

notes: the audio output is multiplied by the accent envelope as well as by the amplitude envelope, so a step is only heard where it falls inside the accent envelope's fall.
a short DELAY setting therefore silences most of the pattern, however dense FILL is made.
nothing steps and no envelope fires until a clock reaches CLK.
